steps.description: Fit DESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~ condition + time + condition:time. Set the reference level of condition (untreated/control level) and of time (t0) explicitly and report both. plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x2x3 bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the treatment effect differ between the two time points — is an interaction question on a 2 conditions x 2 time points design with 3 replicates per cell (12 samples, 12000 genes, /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv plus /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv with condition, time (t0, t1), time_hours). It is answered by a two-factor negative binomial model with a condition:time interaction term, not by two separate per-time-point comparisons.

T1S1 runs the sample structure QC on the raw counts before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition and by time. With a single batch this step exists to expose whether the primary axis of variance is time, condition, or a single departing sample — a fact the interaction fit cannot recover after the fact.

T1S2 fits DESeq2 with design ~condition + time + condition:time on the counts as delivered. The profile states that the counts are gene-level Salmon output with no record of whether the length correction occurred, and there are no per-sample quant.sf files and no average transcript length table in the inputs. The import state is therefore not established: the step fits the count model with no length offset and must state in its output that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can present as differential expression. It must not run tximport on a gene-level table and must not invent a length input. The interaction Wald test is the primary result; the simple effects (treatment effect at t0, treatment effect at t1) are reported beside it at the same threshold, because a gene absent from the interaction list is not shown to have equal effects at both time points. With 3 replicates per cell the interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences and its standard error is the largest in the model — the step states the expected power rather than loosening the threshold.

T1S3 assembles the report: the three result sets side by side with explicit reference levels, shrunken and unshrunken log2 fold changes, MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, the counts of NA p-values split by outlier flag versus independent filter, an edgeR quasi-likelihood interaction fit as the robustness check with the overlap reported, and the reproducibility record. No enrichment step is planned: the question asks whether the effect differs between time points, and gene-set analysis was not requested.

Benjamini-Hochberg within contrast with independent filtering
interaction report with simple effects, diagnostics, power statement, session info

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

With an interaction question and three or fewer replicates in a cell of the design, the interaction term has low power. The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, thus its standard error is larger than the standard error of a main effect at the same replicate number. Keep the interaction test as the primary result, but report the simple effects in each level beside it, with the same threshold. State the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene that is absent from the interaction list is not shown to have the same effect in both levels.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
